review_note: Supply-chain disruption and input-cost recovery lags were specific but contained. Underlying EBIT margin recovered, free cash flow was strong, net debt fell by more than £100m and covenant leverage reduced to 0.8x, while revenue and earnings reached records, providing multiple strong quantified contrary indicators.

Construction-market slowing, 2% lower overall volumes and operating-gearing pressure were repeated and quantified. Underlying EBIT margin fell 60bps to 10.5%; working capital absorbed £9m and free-cash-flow conversion remained below target at 39%, although it improved from 29%. Pricing more than offset volume decline, revenue grew 7%, leverage reduced to 0.5x and liquidity exceeded £475m, providing strong offsets.

Operational pressure was limited largely to routine market and vendor risks. Gross profit as a percentage of gross invoiced income fell about 160bps because of business mix, although adjusted operating profit as a percentage of gross profit improved. Gross profit and adjusted operating profit grew 13.1% and 18.1%, cash conversion was 131%, year-end cash was £20.7m with no debt and no external funding was required, providing multiple strong quantified contrary indicators.

Economic and talent pressures were specific but contained. The reported gross-margin decline reflected the IFRS 15 presentation and business mix while gross profit as a percentage of gross invoiced income and adjusted operating profitability improved, so no credible underlying margin deterioration was identified. Cash conversion fell from 131.9% to 84.3% after being negative in the first half, but recovered to 180% in the second half; gross profit and adjusted operating profit grew 20.7% and 21.8%, cash increased to £73m and final and special dividends were proposed, providing strong contrary evidence.
